She discusses Microsoft's focus on providing secure and reliable connectivity wherever users work. The conversation also covers Microsoft's new Surface Mouse and the introduction of haptic technology. Andrews explains how haptic feedback can create more intuitive interactions and enhance productivity experiences across the Windows ecosystem. Additionally, Andrews discusses Microsoft's engagement with the DPAA Global Video Everywhere Summit and shares how hands-on product experiences play an important role in helping customers understand the design, craftsmanship, and functionality of Surface hardware. Throughout the interview, Andrews provides perspectives on AI-powered computing, Surface devices, connectivity, mobility, user experience, hardware innovation, haptics, productivity technology, and the future of personal computing. headline: The Next Stock Market Crash Could Start With Just 3 Companies
summary: Just three companies now account for approximately 21% of the S&P 500's total market capitalization. NVIDIA (NVDA), Apple (AAPL), and Microsoft (MSFT) have become so dominant that their performance could determine the direction of the entire stock market. But what happens if these technology giants stumble? In this episode, 24/7 Wall St. co-founder Doug McIntyre and senior writer Lee Jackson discuss the extraordinary concentration of the S&P 500 and why millions of investors may be taking on more risk than they realize. Much of today's market enthusiasm is driven by artificial intelligence. Companies like NVIDIA, Microsoft, Alphabet (GOOGL), Amazon (AMZN), and Meta Platforms (META) have benefited from enormous expectations for AI growth. But Doug and Lee identify several potential threats to that optimism. They explore how cheaper open-source AI models could challenge industry leaders, why opposition to AI data center construction threatens expansion plans, and how growing electricity demand is driving renewed interest in nuclear power. Most importantly, they discuss what could happen to popular index funds like the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) if the market's largest technology stocks suffer a major sell-off. They also examine whether equal-weight S&P 500 funds could provide investors with better diversification. Is your S&P 500 investment more vulnerable than you think?

headline: CoreWeave, Nebius, and Neoclouds Sink as Market Fear Index Closes in on ‘Extreme Fear’
summary: CoreWeave (CRWV) and Nebius Group (NBIS) are plunging as fears of an AI financing crisis spread across Wall Street. CoreWeave's unsecured bonds recently reached a 15% yield, raising concerns about its massive debt burden and ability to finance future expansion. Investor Chamath Palihapitiya has warned of a potential AI private credit bubble, while Elon Musk responded with a simple "Yikes." Despite these concerns, CoreWeave maintains a $104 billion revenue backlog, and NVIDIA (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang has defended the company. Meanwhile, Cathie Wood's ARK Invest and Cantor Fitzgerald see opportunity in the sell-off. Eric examines Nebius' financing strategy, CoreWeave's soaring interest expenses, and why declining Treasury yields haven't stopped the bleeding. Are CoreWeave and Nebius bargain-priced AI investments, or is Wall Street uncovering a fundamental weakness in the neocloud business model?
